newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Record closing high set on Belgian BEL-20 index.
newsitem.headline: Record closing high set on Belgian BEL-20 index.

text.p: Belgium's Bel-20 index of leading shares ended Thursday at a record closing high ahead of the previous peak on 28 May this year.
The Bel-20 ended 9.55 points or 0.54 percent higher to 1,773.98 points in solid volume.

"We've reached an important all-time closing high in the index," said an analyst. "That partly explains today's heavy volume, but it's not yet persuasive. We'll have to wait for confirmation that resistance levels have been broken."
More than 2.45 billion francs worth of shares changed hands, with Electrabel the highest volume by value, up 1 percent to 7,000 francs with 40,679 shares traded.
"Electrabel with its high dividend is a bit like an equity/bond combination and it benefits from the drop in interest rates yesterday and today," said an analyst.
Holding company Group Bruxelles Lambert was the biggest gainer, up 1.7 percent to 3,900 francs after posting a 12 percent rise in first-half 1996 group net profit.
"GBL results looked good. Its intrinsic value is quite strong," said Corluy analyst Patrick Millecam.
Millecam said the dollar had broken through 1.52 marks and interest rates were coming down.
"It's an ideal climate for equities," he said.

Retailer Delhaize, which posted a first-half group net profit rise of 22 percent earlier this month, was also in demand rising 0.9 percent to 1,715 francs with more than 119,000 shares changing hands.
The Bel-20 ended with 15 stocks up, four down and one unchanged.
